correctness.rationale: For every integer m≥4 the Laplacian has rank m and its column-simplex has uniquely determined barycentric facet normals L^+e_i. Wheel Fourier decomposition gives exact a_m and b_m squared norms, so opposite-facet areas are mV norm. Matrix-tree determinant gives exact V. Summing barycentric ball inequalities fixes the unique incenter and its inradius. Equalizing two vertex-orbit distances gives t_m; strict positivity of the explicit contact probability weights and the weighted-variance identity certify global unique minimum sphere. The Riemann-sum integral gives beta^2=3/(5sqrt5); all limiting constants follow. Independently constructed exact Gram determinants and pseudoinverses passed 132 finite checks. Finite checks are corroborative, not universal proofs.

value.rationale: The nonregular wheel family is canonical in graph-Laplacian polytope geometry. It exhibits a sharp and conceptually different boundary-versus-vertex contact concentration: hub opposite facet has Θ(m^-2) boundary-area share, yet hub vertex receives asymptotically 1/2 of the unique positive optimal-sphere support measure. Exact intrinsic metric values and quadratic roundness with explicit constants are useful comparative invariants; this is not a mere restatement of a matrix-tree volume or small finite graph table.
